concepts.name: Table 6.1: Part A and Part B states of 1950
concepts.description: The nine Part A states and nine Part B states of the 1950 classification.
concepts.idea: Part A had nine former provinces; Part B had nine former princely states or unions.
concepts.rule: Table 6.1 (Territory of India in 1950). Part A: Assam, Bihar, Bombay, Madhya Pradesh, Madras, Orissa, Punjab, United Provinces and West Bengal. Part B: Hyderabad, Jammu and Kashmir, Madhya Bharat, Mysore, Patiala and East Punjab, Rajasthan, Saurashtra, Travancore-Cochin and Vindhya Pradesh. Part A states were former governor's provinces of British India, and Part B states were former princely states with legislatures.
concepts.example: Jammu and Kashmir was a Part B state in 1950.

concepts.name: Table 6.1: Part C states and Part D territory of 1950
concepts.description: The ten Part C states and the single Part D territory.
concepts.idea: Part C had ten centrally administered units and Part D only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
concepts.rule: Part C states of 1950: Ajmer, Bhopal, Bilaspur, Cooch-Behar, Coorg, Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Kutch, Manipur and Tripura. These were former chief commissioners' provinces of British India and some princely states, and were centrally administered. Part D: Andaman and Nicobar Islands. In all there were 29 units: 9 in Part A, 9 in Part B, 10 in Part C and 1 in Part D.
concepts.example: Delhi and Himachal Pradesh were Part C states in 1950.

concepts.name: Table 6.2: states and union territories in 1956
concepts.description: The fourteen states and six union territories of 1 November 1956.
concepts.idea: The 1956 reorganisation gave 14 states and 6 union territories.
concepts.rule: Table 6.2 (1956). States: Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Bombay, Jammu and Kashmir, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Madras, Mysore, Orissa, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal. Union territories: Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands, Manipur and Tripura. The Act created Kerala by merging Travancore-Cochin with Malabar district and Kasaragod; created Andhra Pradesh by merging Telugu-speaking areas of Hyderabad with Andhra; merged Madhya Bharat, Vindhya Pradesh and Bhopal into Madhya Pradesh; merged Saurashtra and Kutch into Bombay; Coorg into Mysore; Pepsu into Punjab; Ajmer into Rajasthan; and created the union territory of Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands from Madras.
concepts.example: Kerala was one of the 14 states of 1956.

concepts.name: Further details on the making of states and union territories
concepts.description: Additional facts on Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Andhra and Telangana.
concepts.idea: Several states and union territories passed through special stages before their present status.
concepts.rule: Dadra and Nagar Haveli: liberated from Portugal in 1954, administered by an administrator chosen by the people till 1961, made a union territory by the 10th Amendment (1961). Goa, Daman and Diu: police action 1961; union territory by the 12th Amendment (1962); Goa a state in 1987. Puducherry: French handed over in 1954; acquired territory till the 14th Amendment (1962). Nagaland: placed under the Governor of Assam in 1961 before statehood in 1963 as the 16th state. Haryana: 17th state in 1966 after the Akali Dal demanded a Punjabi Suba under Master Tara Singh; the Shah Commission recommended Punjabi areas as Punjab, Hindi areas as Haryana and hill areas merged with Himachal. Himachal Pradesh became the 18th state in 1971. Meghalaya: the 22nd Amendment (1969) made it an autonomous state within Assam before full statehood in 1972 (21st state); Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh (formerly NEFA) became union territories in 1972. Sikkim: Chogyal rule; protectorate after 1947; 35th Amendment (1974) added Article 2A and the Tenth Schedule for an associate state; 36th Amendment (1975) made it the 22nd state with Article 371F. Mizoram Peace Accord (1986) with the Mizo National Front led to statehood in 1987. Andhra: Kurnool capital and High Court at Guntur in 1953; Hyderabad became the capital in 1956; the 2014 Act formed Telangana.
concepts.example: The Shah Commission of 1966 recommended the division of Punjab.
